Does Brad Pitt die in The Tree of Life?

He plays Mr. O'Brien.

Want to guess first?

Revealing shows the answer, the scene, and a clip if we have one.

No. It's his son who dies; he outlives the boy.

The film opens with Mr. and Mrs. O'Brien receiving the telegram that their 19-year-old son R.L. has died in the 1960s, and the rest unfolds as older son Jack's memories of a 1950s Texas childhood under his stern, frustrated father. Mr. O'Brien, an engineer and thwarted musician, loses a patent suit and his plant closes, and in a moment of humility asks Jack's forgiveness before the family moves away. He is last seen alive, and in the film's beach-of-eternity coda the whole family, R.L. included, is reunited.

The film's central death is R.L.'s, delivered by telegram in the opening minutes. The afterlife/beach sequence is metaphysical, not a literal death of Mr. O'Brien.
